m1.speaker: mei
m1.text: Another of HIS. The veiled one came first, then you. He always sends the masked ones before the blade.

m2.speaker: mei
m2.text: My husband was the Lamplighter's apprentice. When he died, the Lamplighter carried his soul through the fog so it wouldn't be lost. I saw it. I saw him smile.

choices.text: A boy named Tobi says his sister is lost in the fog.
My master says the Lamplighter burns souls.

m_sorry.speaker: mei
m_sorry.text: ...Thank you. No one has said that to me in this city. Not once. Be careful who you believe, samurai. Lamps don't burn the things they guide.

m_counter.speaker: mei
m_counter.text: Then your master has never stood in the fog and watched someone come home.

lantern.speaker: mei
lantern.text: Suzu. Of course. The fog keeps the lost the way a pocket keeps coins.

lantern2.speaker: mei
lantern2.text: My husband's lantern still burns in the old cellar past the kiln, in the south-east. No one has dared touch it since he died. A lit lamp is a road home. Take it to the boy.

after.speaker: mei
after.text: The fog is thicker since you came. That isn't a coincidence.

post.speaker: narrator
post.text: The fog has thickened since the Lamplighter fell. Somewhere in it, someone is calling a name and getting no answer.

post2.speaker: mei
post2.text: He walked them home for a hundred years. Who walks them now, samurai?

vow.speaker: mei
vow.text: Then take his lantern pole too. It drank a thunderstorm once - it can drink a little fog. Don't you dare put it down.

post_idk.speaker: mei
post_idk.text: Neither do I. That's what frightens me.

after_vow.speaker: mei
after_vow.text: Keep it lit. That's all he ever did. That's all any of us can do.

after_all.speaker: mei
after_all.text: Go. Someone is waiting at the end of your road too.
